generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, active revision matters because every subject rewards knowledge you can use, not just recognise. A sport science student rereading a physiology chapter, a coaching student skimming a session plan, and a management student looking over participation figures all feel the same false comfort. The subjects differ in their evidence, from lab data to coaching judgement to policy, yet the fix is shared: rebuild the idea from memory, sketch it, and test yourself until you can reproduce it.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport and exercise science students set aside the same hours to revise the same topic: the three energy systems that fuel exercise.

Tom spends the time reading. He reads the chapter twice and highlights the key terms, from the phosphagen system to aerobic metabolism. It feels like steady progress, and he covers every page. But he produces nothing: no diagram of the pathways, no self-test, no explanation in his own words. When a past question asks him to compare the systems, the material feels familiar yet strangely hard to reproduce. This is passive revision.

Amara reads the same chapter once, then closes it. She rebuilds the three systems from memory as a labelled diagram, turns each gap into a test question, and explains aloud how they overlap during a sprint. Each gap that surfaces sends her back to the chapter with a purpose. By the end she can reproduce and compare the systems, not just recognise them. This is active revision.

Both spent the same hours. Only Amara turned those hours into knowledge that would survive the exam, by producing and testing rather than only reading.
generatedProse.summary: Active revision in the School of Sport is a different kind of work with your material, not just more time on it. Whether your evidence is lab data, a session plan or participation figures, you can now contrast active and passive revision and explain why producing and testing an idea deepens it. You can also judge whether an approach is truly active. The next lesson turns this into the specific techniques you can choose from.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's revision active rather than passive?

items.text: She rebuilt the energy systems from memory and tested herself, returning to the chapter only to fix gaps.
She spent more hours revising than Tom.
She read the chapter more carefully than Tom.
She highlighted the key terms in the textbook.

feedback.correct: That's right. Producing and testing the systems, then targeting the chapter, is what made it active.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara DID with the material, beyond reading it.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara rebuilt the energy systems from memory and tested herself, returning to the chapter only to fix gaps. Extra hours, careful reading and highlighting are all still passive.
